blocks.content: FROM sets the base image a Dockerfile builds on top of, and is almost always the very first instruction in the file.
FROM tells Docker which existing image to start from, everything after it in the Dockerfile adds layers on top of that base, exactly as covered in the Base Image topic from the previous module.

blocks.alt: FROM picks the starting point for everything else

blocks.content:
FROM node:18
FROM python:3.11-slim
FROM ubuntu:22.04

code.content:

FROM python:3.11-slim
FROM ubuntu:22.04

codes.dockerfile:
FROM node:18
FROM python:3.11-slim
FROM ubuntu:22.04

blocks.content: Every Dockerfile needs a starting point before any other instruction makes sense, so FROM is (barring comments or ARG declarations used only to parameterize the base image itself) the first real instruction in the file.
3. Multiple FROM Lines for Multi-Stage Builds
blocks.text: 3. Multiple FROM Lines for Multi-Stage Builds

blocks.content: A Dockerfile is not limited to one FROM, multi-stage builds (introduced conceptually in the previous module, mechanics covered fully in Docker Build) use several FROM lines, each starting a new, independent stage.

blocks.alt: One FROM per stage, in a multi-stage build

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: FROM sets the base image everything else in the Dockerfile builds on top of, and is almost always the opening instruction.
A Dockerfile can have multiple FROM lines, one per stage, when using a multi-stage build.
